lede: The biggest thing on the civic calendar this week is the San Miguel County BOCC meeting on August 5th, where commissioners will hold public hearings on three Land Use Code amendments — including changes to how 'Qualified Owner' is defined in affordable housing rules, a wildfire areas update, and a continued hearing on nonconforming lots. That same day, the Ouray County Planning Commission meets virtually to work through possible changes to their Land Use Code definitions section, and TMVOA takes up amendments to its fiscal policies at its July 31st board meeting. On the lighter side, the San Miguel Basin Fair and Rodeo kicks off Friday alongside a free Jungle Book show at the Sheridan.

notable.stake: Public hearings on three Land Use Code amendments, including affordable housing ownership rules.
Land Use Code definitions are being rewritten — definitions determine what rules actually mean.
Proposed amendments to TMVOA fiscal policies up for formal action.
